statement: cejel #626's v27 A1 restore reader admitted a restore by its spelling: any `items.extend(x)` after the clear, from a source it could not show to be empty, handed back v17's credit and the note said the hook "puts the collected items back". Each review round found another look-alike (an aliased and cleared copy, `saved[5:5]`, `list(items)[:0]`, a helper adding `src * 0`) and added one more exclusion, so the reader kept defaulting to credit for every shape nobody had listed yet. The fix (#631) inverts the default: a restore counts only in a closed list of shapes the reader proves, an emptying counts only where it proves the list stays empty, and everything else goes to a named third outcome, "not read", which makes no claim and says why in the note. Rule: when a reader decides between two claims, give it a third outcome that says it could not decide, and send to that outcome everything outside what it proves. Do not grow a list of exclusions in front of a default.

In goal_cejel_v27_a1_restore_proof_and_hookwrapper_2026-11-02, item F re-measured cejel #626's last code round (`0aa1116b8`) on the 393 synthetic repositories #626's records name, and every report was byte-identical to the round's parent. That only shows the round regressed nothing: those 393 repositories were built from the fixture files at `26a7d4795`, before the round's own fixtures existed, so none of them holds a shape the round changes. A re-measure on a corpus frozen before a change can show that the change moved nothing else, but never that it did what it was for. Rule: when you report a re-measure, name the commit the corpus was built from, say whether it contains the change's own fixtures, and do not present byte-identity as evidence that the change works.
